title: Plot generation scripts for permanent benchmarks
description:
Add plot generation scripts that turn the criterion JSON outputs (T10, S1, S2, S3, S5) into publication-grade figures.

## Background

The reproducible benchmark artefact (S6) needs PNG/SVG plots of: (a) log-time vs $n$ for the F_3 permanent paths (reference, bipedal, SIMD, parallel), (b) parallel scaling vs core count, (c) AVX2-vs-AVX-512 cross-CPU bars, (d) GPU vs CPU crossover. This issue lands the plotting scripts under `scripts/plot_permanent_*.py` (matplotlib) or `scripts/plot_permanent_*.rs` (plotters), reading from the criterion JSON paths in `target/criterion/` or the simulation CSVs in `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/`.

The choice of matplotlib vs plotters is left to the implementer; the constraint is that the script must be deterministically reproducible.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `scripts/plot_permanent_*` scripts exist (matplotlib or plotters; document the choice in the script header).
- [ ] [hard] At least four figure types are produced: (a) log-time vs $n$ for the F_3 permanent paths (see 2026-05-15 amendment a for the impl-series enumeration that materially exists in S1 + S2), (b) parallel-scaling, (c) AVX2-vs-AVX-512 cross-CPU bars (see 2026-05-15 amendment b for the dev-host AVX-512 hardware constraint), (d) GPU-vs-CPU.
- [ ] [hard] Figures are written to `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/figures/` with deterministic file names.
- [ ] [hard] Running the scripts twice produces bit-identical output (after timestamp normalisation, if any).
- [ ] [hard] Scripts read from the conventional CSV locations recorded in S1/S2/S3/S5 (S4 dropped per 2026-05-15 amendment c — same hardware constraint as figure (c)); missing input data produces a clear error, not a partial figure.

## Amendment 2026-05-15a — Figure (a) impl-series enumeration

The original criterion 2(a) listed four series: "reference, bipedal, SIMD, parallel". After consulting the upstream benchmark inputs:

- `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s1_speedup-2026-05-11.csv` columns: `impl ∈ {permanent_mod3_reference, permanent_bipedal3_simd}` — i.e., **S1 has only two distinct impl curves**, not three. The "bipedal" scalar fallback path (used at runtime only when AVX2 is unavailable) is exercised in unit tests (`test_simd_vs_scalar_n24` and friends) but not separately benchmarked because the production dispatch on every supported host selects the SIMD path.
- `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s2_parallel_scaling-2026-05-11.csv` adds the parallel path at `n ∈ {28, 32, 36}` with thread counts `{1, 2, 4, 8, 12}`.

**Amended scope for figure (a):** the figure overlays the three series that materially exist in the benchmark CSVs:

1. `permanent_mod3_reference` (S1)
2. `permanent_bipedal3_simd` (S1) — the "bipedal-SIMD" production path; on the dev host this is the only bipedal variant exercised, so the original "bipedal" and "SIMD" entries in the criterion's series list collapse into this single curve.
3. `permanent_bipedal3_parallel` (S2 at max thread count = 12)

A separately-benchmarked scalar bipedal path would require either a new S1' run with SIMD disabled (substantial work) or a runtime-toggle path on the same dev host. Neither is in this epic's scope; it is recorded as a future follow-up at criterion-fidelity-tier (not in scope for `ae82bd73`).

## Amendment 2026-05-15b — Figure (c) AVX-512 hardware constraint (lead-direct per 363556e6 precedent)

Criterion 2 bullet (c) names "AVX2-vs-AVX-512 cross-CPU bars". The dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, Zen 3) has AVX2 but no AVX-512; collecting AVX-512 measurements would require a different host class.

**Precedent (`363556e6` "Cross-CPU portability sweep on AVX2-only dev host"):** that issue's title was amended in the same way during W3, deferring the AVX-512 axis to the separately-tracked future issue `f8d230ef`. The S3 CSV consumed by this issue's figure (c) (`dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s3_cross_cpu-2026-05-12.csv`) is the artefact `363556e6` produced under that amendment — i.e., it inherits the AVX-512 deferral by construction.

**Amended scope for figure (c):** the implementation produces an AVX2-vs-scalar cross-impl bar chart (the AVX2-vs-AVX-512 contrast as it materialises on the dev host) and annotates the AVX-512 axis as "N/A (dev host: AVX2 only)" inline on the figure. When AVX-512 hardware becomes available and `f8d230ef` lands its S3' measurement, the `plot_cross_cpu` function in `scripts/plot_permanent_benchmarks.py` already accepts a third `avx512_impl` series via its substring classifier and will render the third bar set without further changes.

**Why amendment-not-escalation here:** the constraint is `363556e6`-precedented and the amendment scope (AVX-512 deferral with explicit follow-up to `f8d230ef`) matches that precedent's resolution exactly. No new architectural decision; the precedent already exists.

## Amendment 2026-05-15c — S4 input dropped (same hardware constraint as figure (c))

The original criterion 5 named S1/S2/S3/**S4**/S5 as conventional CSV inputs. S4 was the planned AVX-512 cross-CPU sweep that was deferred to `f8d230ef` for the same hardware reason that drives amendment 2026-05-15b (the dev host has no AVX-512). No S4 CSV was produced under this epic; the input list collapses to S1/S2/S3/S5.

When `f8d230ef` produces an S4 CSV on a future AVX-512 host, the `plot_cross_cpu` function in `scripts/plot_permanent_benchmarks.py` accepts an `avx512_impl` series automatically (substring classifier); a follow-up commit can wire an `S4_FILENAME` constant and pre-flight entry into the script without redesign.
